tags.name: Files
tags.description: Spaces, browsing, search, categories/tags, folder operations, downloads with HTTP Range support, thumbnails, ZIP downloads, simple uploads and rescans.

tags.name: Uploads
tags.description: Resumable uploads using the tus 1.0.0 protocol (extensions: creation, termination, checksum, expiration). Use these for anything large.

tags.name: Trash
tags.description: Trashed files: list, restore, delete permanently, empty. Trash is purged automatically after `files.trash_retention_days`.

tags.name: Backup
tags.description: Devices of the desktop backup utility: the folders each device keeps synced into Files, and sync run reports.

get.description:
Spaces the caller can read: the home space first (created on demand), then libraries shared with the user (or all libraries for admins).

**Scope:** `files:read`

Lists one directory: its entry, breadcrumbs and a page of children (directories first).

**Scope:** `files:read`

parameters.name: space_id
parameters.description: Space to browse (default: the caller's home space).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Directory path in the space (`""` = root).

get.description:
Every entry below `path`, streamed as one JSON document, for sync clients such as the desktop backup utility. Subtrees with more than 200 000 entries are rejected with 413 — sync a narrower path.

**Scope:** `files:read`

Full-text search (name, path, tags) and filters across every space the caller can read.

**Scope:** `files:read`

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search text (FTS on name/path/tags). Optional when filtering.

patch.description:
Renames (`name`) and/or sets category, subcategory and tags.

**Scope:** `files:write`

409.description: The new name already exists in the directory.

delete.summary: Move an entry to the trash

409.description: Name already exists — also when this server's disk is not case-sensitive and a sibling differs only in case (`details.existing_name`).

post.description:
Moves files/folders to another directory (possibly in another space). Each item succeeds or fails individually; moving a folder into itself fails. `overwrite` moves the existing destination entry to the trash first. Moves are renames on disk (copy + delete across volumes) and keep entry IDs; moving into a home space transfers ownership (and quota) to its owner. The destination folder must exist (404 otherwise).

**Scope:** `files:write`

Copies files/folders (recursively). New entries get new IDs. Counts against the quota of the destination owner (the home owner, or the caller in libraries). Folders with more than 200 000 entries are refused per item.

**Scope:** `files:write`

post.summary: Move several entries to the trash

post.description:
Sets category/subcategory and adds/removes tags on many entries at once. Entries the caller cannot write are reported in `errors` and skipped. Setting `category` without `subcategory` clears subcategories that do not belong to the new category.

**Scope:** `files:write`

get.description:
File bytes with `Range`, `If-Range` and `ETag` support (seekable video/audio). `Content-Disposition` is
`attachment` when `download=1`; otherwise `inline` only for safe types (images, video, audio, PDF, `text/plain`) and
`attachment` for everything else — `text/html` and SVG are **always** served as attachments.

Responses carry `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox …`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a strong `ETag` derived from id, size and modification time; active types (HTML, SVG, XML, JavaScript) are sent as `application/octet-stream`. Inline PDFs may be framed by the same origin (web UI preview). Folders answer 400 (use `/zip`).

**Scope:** `files:read` · also accepts `?access_token=`

200.description: The file content with its detected `Content-Type`.

206.description: Partial content for a satisfiable `Range` request.

get.description:
JPEG thumbnail. Images are thumbnailed in pure Go (JPEG/PNG/GIF, ≤ 50 MP); video thumbnails need ffmpeg. 404 when none exists (`has_thumbnail: false`). Thumbnails are cached on disk and served with `Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600` and an `ETag`; video thumbnails are taken at 10 % of the duration when ffmpeg is available and `media.auto_thumbnails` is on.

**Scope:** `files:read` · also accepts `?access_token=`

Streams a ZIP archive of the folder (store-only for already-compressed media). Entries are placed under `<folder name>/`; already-compressed formats are stored, others deflated. Folders with more than 200 000 entries answer 413. Not resumable.

**Scope:** `files:read`

post.description:
Uploads one file from the raw request body. `Content-Length` is required; the body is capped at
`files.max_upload_bytes`, or 2 GiB when that is unlimited. For large files or unreliable links use the resumable
**Uploads** (tus) endpoints. The file is written to a temp file and committed atomically.

**Scope:** `files:write`

parameters.name: overwrite
parameters.description: Replace an existing file of the same name (default false → 409).

parameters.name: mod_time
parameters.description: Modification time to record (e.g. from the source file).

400.description: `Content-Length` missing (chunked bodies are refused) or the body length differs from it.

409.description: A file with that name exists and `overwrite` is false.

post.description:
Reconciles the file index with what is on disk (files added/removed outside Ludworks) in a background job: new files are indexed, changed ones updated, vanished ones removed, and `file.*` events are published. Symbolic links and names that are not valid Ludworks names are skipped. 404 when `path` is not a folder.

**Scope:** `files:write`

get.description:
The caller's trash (home space trash plus entries they trashed in writable libraries), most recently trashed first. Only trashed roots are listed (a trashed folder's contents come back with it on restore). `path` and `original_path` are the location the entry had before it was trashed. Entries older than `files.trash_retention_days` are purged hourly.

**Scope:** `files:read`

delete.description:
Permanently deletes everything in the caller's trash: the trash of their home space plus what they trashed in libraries they can write. `deleted` counts every removed entry including folder contents.

**Scope:** `files:write`

post.description:
Restores the entry (and its contents) to its original location, recreating missing parent folders.

**Scope:** `files:write`

parameters.name: rename
parameters.description: `1` restores under a free name if the original name is taken.

409.description: Original name is taken; retry with `rename=1`.

get.description:
Categories and subcategories used to tag files (`movie`, `tv`, `music`, `image`, `game`, `document`, `software`, `other` by default).

**Scope:** `auth`

put.description:
Replaces the whole taxonomy. Files keep their stored slugs even if a category is removed.

**Scope:** `admin`

post.description:
Creates a shared library (e.g. "Family Media") with per-user or everyone (`*`) read/write access.

**Scope:** `admin`

409.description: A space with that name exists.

patch.summary: Rename a library / replace its members

delete.description:
Refused with 409 while the space contains files, unless `force=true` (which deletes the files permanently).

**Scope:** `admin`

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Delete even if the space is not empty.

put.description:
Renames the device and/or replaces its synced folder list.

**Scope:** `files:write`

delete.description:
Removes the device record. Already uploaded files are **not** touched.

**Scope:** `files:write`

post.description:
Called by the backup utility at the start (`running`) and end (`ok`/`error`) of a sync run; shown in the web UI.

**Scope:** `files:write`

options.description:
Advertises the tus version, extensions, checksum algorithms and maximum size. (`Tus-Resumable` is not required on OPTIONS.)

**Scope:** `public`

Tus-Max-Size.description: Maximum upload size in bytes (only when `files.max_upload_bytes` > 0).

post.description:
Creates an upload (tus `creation`). Send no body. `Upload-Metadata` is a comma-separated list of
`key base64(value)` pairs with keys `filename` (required), `space_id` (required), `path` (target dir, default `""`),
`overwrite` (`1`/`0`), `mod_time` (RFC 3339), `category`, `subcategory`, `tags` (comma-separated) and `mime`.

Permission, file name, quota and free disk space (`Upload-Length` + 1 GiB headroom) are checked **now**, so a
too-large upload fails before any byte is sent. `Upload-Defer-Length` is not supported.

**Scope:** `files:write`

201.description: Upload created. PATCH the data to `Location`.

Upload-Expires.description: RFC 7231 date after which the incomplete upload is purged (`files.upload_expiry_hours`).

Ludworks-File-Id.description: Only for `Upload-Length: 0`: the empty file is committed immediately.

Ludworks-File-Path.description: Space-relative path of the committed file, each segment percent-encoded (RFC 3986) so the header stays ASCII.

400.description: Invalid `Upload-Length`, malformed `Upload-Metadata`, `Upload-Defer-Length` sent, or a request body sent (creation-with-upload is not supported).

409.description: Target exists (or is a folder) and `overwrite` is not `1`, a path component is a file, or the caller already has 1000 incomplete uploads.

412.description: Missing or unsupported `Tus-Resumable` (response carries `Tus-Version: 1.0.0`); error code `precondition_failed`.

507.description: `quota_exceeded` (the quota counts every file the owner owns, trash included, plus their other incomplete uploads) or `insufficient_storage` (needs `Upload-Length` + 1 GiB free).

get.description:
Non-tus convenience endpoint: the caller's unfinished, unexpired uploads (newest first, at most 1000) (to resume or cancel them).

**Scope:** `files:write`

head.description:
Returns how many bytes the server has, so an interrupted upload can continue from there.

**Scope:** `files:write`

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Upload ID (last segment of the `Location` returned at creation).

200.description: Current state. A completed upload stays queryable for 24 h; it reports `Upload-Offset` = `Upload-Length` plus the `Ludworks-File-*` headers, so a client whose final PATCH response was lost learns the result.

Ludworks-File-Id.description: ID of the committed `Entry` (only once the upload is complete).

Ludworks-File-Path.description: Space-relative path of the committed file, each segment percent-encoded (RFC 3986) so the header stays ASCII.

404.description: Unknown upload (or owned by another user)

patch.description:
Appends the body at `Upload-Offset` (which must equal the server's current offset, else 409). With
`Upload-Checksum: sha256 <base64>` (or `sha1`) the chunk is verified and discarded on mismatch (status 460).
Data is fsynced at the end of each chunk. Recommended chunk size 8–64 MiB.

When the final byte arrives the file is committed atomically into the target directory and the response carries
`Ludworks-File-Id` and `Ludworks-File-Path` (percent-encoded segments). With `overwrite` an existing file keeps its entry ID and its
previous version goes to the trash. Repeating the final PATCH (empty body at `Upload-Offset` = `Upload-Length`) is idempotent and
also retries a commit that failed with 507.

Without `Upload-Checksum`, the bytes of an interrupted chunk that did arrive are kept (resume from HEAD); with a checksum an
incomplete chunk is discarded. A stalled body times out after 2 minutes without data. Each successful PATCH extends `Upload-Expires`.

**Scope:** `files:write`

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Upload ID (last segment of the `Location` returned at creation).

parameters.name: Upload-Checksum
parameters.description: `<algorithm> <base64 digest>` of this chunk, algorithm `sha1` or `sha256`.

Ludworks-File-Id.description: Only on the final chunk: ID of the committed `Entry`.

Ludworks-File-Path.description: Space-relative path of the committed file, each segment percent-encoded (RFC 3986) so the header stays ASCII.

400.description: Missing/invalid headers, an unsupported checksum algorithm, or a body that ended early (the client disconnected or sent fewer bytes than `Content-Length`; the bytes that arrived are kept or discarded as described above).

409.description: `Upload-Offset` does not match the server offset (the response carries the current `Upload-Offset`) — HEAD and resume. Also returned when the target name was taken by another file before the commit; the upload is then discarded.

413.description: The chunk extends beyond `Upload-Length`; it was discarded.

423.description: Another request is currently writing to this upload (concurrent PATCH); retry shortly. Error code `locked`.

460.description: Checksum mismatch; the chunk was discarded.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Upload ID (last segment of the `Location` returned at creation).

423.description: Another request is currently writing to this upload (concurrent PATCH); retry shortly. Error code `locked`.

items.description: Children of `dir`; directories first, then the requested sort.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 or `""` if not computed yet.

name.description: New name (rename in place). File or folder name: ≤ 255 bytes UTF-8, no `/ \ NUL` or control characters, not `.`/`..`, no trailing dot/space, not a Windows reserved device name (CON, NUL, COM1…).

path.description: Space-relative directory path, `/`-separated without leading slash; `""` = space root.

name.description: File or folder name: ≤ 255 bytes UTF-8, no `/ \ NUL` or control characters, not `.`/`..`, no trailing dot/space, not a Windows reserved device name (CON, NUL, COM1…).

dest_path.description: Space-relative directory path, `/`-separated without leading slash; `""` = space root.

on_conflict.description: What to do when the destination name exists: fail that item, rename (`name (1).ext`), or overwrite.

FilesItemError.description: Per-item failure of a bulk operation.

original_path.description: Path the entry had before it was trashed.

FilesTrashPage.description: A page of trashed entries, most recently trashed first.

icon.description: Icon name from the web UI icon set (e.g. `film`, `tv`, `music`, `image`, `gamepad`).

user_id.description: User ID, or `*` for every user.

file_count.description: Number of files (excluding folders and trash).

FilesLibrarySpace.description: A library space as seen by admins (includes members).

members.description: Who may access the library. Admins always have write access.

local_path.description: Folder on the device, as the device reports it (e.g. `C:\Users\alice\Pictures`).

platform.description: Device platform as reported by the client.

bytes_uploaded.description: Bytes uploaded by the last run.

files_uploaded.description: Files uploaded by the last run.

folders.description: Replaces the folder list. Each remote space must be writable by the caller.

FilesUpload.description: An incomplete resumable upload of the caller.

errors.description: Entries that were not found, not writable or invalid (e.g. a subcategory that does not belong to their category).
